sections.h2: Who to call in Long County
sections.html:
Three offices share the work in Ludowici, and all three sit on McDonald Street. One sets values, one sends and collects bills, and one votes the county rate. Knowing which desk answers which question saves you a round of phone transfers.

  • Long County Tax Assessor's Office: 285 S McDonald St, Ludowici, GA 31316. Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm. Phone (912) 545-9111. The office links to the qPublic parcel search and a digest archive that goes back to 2016.
  • Long County Tax Commissioner: P.O. Box 628, 285 South McDonald Street, Ludowici, GA 31316. Phone 912-545-2127. Payments now run through a newer site, and the older taxpayer search tab no longer takes them.
  • Long County Board of Commissioners: 468 S. McDonald Street, Ludowici. The board sets the county millage rate at a called meeting. The office works Monday through Thursday, 8:30am to 5:00pm, and has been closed on Fridays since January 26, 2026.

The state's Department of Revenue splits the questions the same way. Bills and payments go to the commissioner. Value, exemption and appeal questions go to the assessors. Call the wrong desk and you will get a quick referral to the right one.

Long County is rural, mostly farm and forest, with Ludowici as its only city and the county seat. Fort Stewart takes up the northern tip and supplies civilian jobs and a steady stream of renters and buyers. Aimar, Beards Creek, Donald and Tibet are unincorporated, so owners there deal with the county for permits and tax questions.

The county grew fast. Its mid-2025 estimate is 21,557 residents, up from 16,168 in the 2020 count. There are 7,798 housing units, and 65.2% of homes are owner-occupied. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $218,300. Builders pulled 275 permits in 2025, and new construction and added improvements feed the tax digest.

The county's five-year history shows a taxable base that keeps growing and a county rate that moves in steps. The net digest rose from about $328.8 million in 2021 to about $546.0 million in the 2026 figures. Net maintenance and operation millage is 17.802 mills in the 2026 presentation.

The county's levy reflects reductions from Property Tax Relief Local Option Sales Tax proceeds, also called FLOST, which are applied against property tax. County voters approved FLOST in 2025, and the combined sales tax rate in Long County became 9% on January 1, 2026.

The 2025 rate came with a notice of a tentative increase of 20.72 percent: 18.707 mills against 15.496 mills without the increase. School and state levies sit on top of the county figure, so the rate on your own bill is the one that counts.

The 2026 digest has a gross figure of $791,914,814 and exemptions of $245,871,061, which leaves the net value in the table. Exemptions stood at $104,458,820 in 2024 and $234,837,877 in 2025, so the jump in the net base in 2025 came with a much larger exempt share. Real and personal property made up $774,693,757 of the 2026 gross. Motor vehicles, mobile homes and timber are small slices.

Long County due dates follow the digest rather than a fixed calendar date. For the 2025 bills, real estate taxes were due May 12, 2026, and mobile home taxes were due June 1, 2026 instead of the usual April 1, because the digest came out late. The state default is December 20, or 60 days from billing, and a county may choose another date.

Read the due date printed on your bill, and ask the commissioner's office when the next mailing goes out.

  • Property returns are accepted from January 1 through April 1.
  • Mobile home tax is normally due April 1.
  • Payment runs through the newer site linked from the commissioner's page.

You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice is mailed. Put the appeal on paper for the Long County assessors, using the uniform form the state provides.

That first filing is where you pick a route: the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. State revenue officials have no power to overrule any of those bodies, or Superior Court, on one property's appraisal. Where a county has adopted a written policy accepting electronic service, the appeal may be emailed. Ask the assessors whether Long County has done so, and use longcoappr@longcountyga.gov if it has.

Valid grounds include whether the property is taxable, its value, equal treatment with similar parcels, or a turned-down exemption. Before filing, pull your parcel on qPublic and compare it with recent sales nearby. Bring those sales to the conversation with the assessors.

The standard state homestead exemption takes $2,000 off the assessed value, which Georgia sets at 40% of market value. The home must be your main residence on January 1.

  • Some counties take homestead filings at the commissioner's desk and others at the assessors. Ask Long County which one applies.
  • Local exemptions can exceed the state one. The assessors can list them with their age and income limits.
  • Farm, timber and conservation assessments rest on a covenant signed with the assessors, so confirm eligibility before assuming acreage qualifies.

If you added a room, a barn or a garage, compare your January 1 value with the parcel record to make sure the improvement is described correctly.

The January 1 title holder owes the full year, and a sale on January 2 changes nothing with the state. No refund goes to partial-year owners, so buyer and seller divide the bill in the sales contract.

  1. Ask the commissioner for a payoff amount that includes any interest or penalty.
  2. Give the closing attorney the current bill and that payoff figure.
  3. Check whether a tax lien (a fi fa) has been recorded against the parcel. Payoff or release is needed before a buyer can take clean title.
  4. If a bill reaches you after closing, forward it to the new owner.

An inherited, behind-on-tax or tenant-occupied house in Long County follows the same steps. A cash buyer can close quickly, but the lien still has to be paid at the table. Call early, since a figure quoted weeks ahead can grow as interest adds up.

faqs.q: Which Long County office answers questions about my bill?
faqs.a: Billing and payment questions go to the Tax Commissioner at 912-545-2127, or by mail to P.O. Box 628 in Ludowici. Value, exemption and appeal questions go to the Tax Assessor's Office at (912) 545-9111.

faqs.q: How long is the Long County assessment appeal window?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the day the notice was mailed. File on paper with the county assessors and name your chosen route in that first filing.

faqs.q: Has the Long County millage rate gone up?
faqs.a: Net M&O millage was 14.738 in 2023, 18.707 in 2024 and 2025, and 17.802 in the 2026 presentation. Sales tax relief proceeds are applied against the levy, so use the rate on your bill.

faqs.q: Is any tax refunded when a Long County home sells mid-year?
faqs.a: No. The January 1 owner owes the whole year, so the buyer and seller settle the split in the sales contract.

faqs.q: Where can I search a Long County parcel online?
faqs.a: Use the qPublic property search linked from the Tax Assessor's page. It shows parcel records, and the assessors' office can explain any value you find.
